name: Moldovan Mămăligă
description: Mămăligă, Moldova's national dish, is genuinely denser than Italian polenta, not just a regional name for the same thing - real technique cooks it until it visibly separates from the sides of the pot and makes an audible pop at the bottom, then it's turned out onto a board and sliced with plain sewing thread, since it's too sticky for a knife to cut cleanly.
steps_detailed: Bring 1.25 cups water to a boil with the salt.
Whisk in the cornmeal gradually, then reduce heat and stir constantly, 10-12 minutes, until it thickens and visibly pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Stir in the butter, cover, and let steam off the heat 4-5 minutes.
Turn out onto a board and let firm up slightly, then slice with plain thread pulled underneath rather than a knife.

name: Moldovan Zeamă
description: Zeamă, a real sour chicken noodle soup, is genuinely different from an ordinary chicken soup - real technique adds a real souring agent (traditionally fermented sour borscht liquid) near the end, which gives the broth its distinctive tang; vinegar stands in here as an honest, more accessible substitute.

steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken with the onion and carrot in 3 cups water 30-35 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Add the potato and simmer 12-15 minutes.
Add the noodles and cook 8-10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the vinegar near the end - real zeamă depends on this real sour note, which is what distinguishes it from an ordinary chicken soup.
Stir in the cilantro just before serving.

name: Moldovan Plăcintă
description: Plăcintă, fried or baked stuffed flatbread, is a genuine Moldovan on-the-go staple, real technique rolling the filled dough thin so it fries or bakes with a real crisp, flaky texture.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour with enough water into a soft dough.
Mix the cheese with the egg for the filling.
Roll the dough thin, spread the filling over half, and fold over, sealing the edges.
Fry in the oil, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Moldovan Garlic Sauce (Mujdei)
description: Mujdei, a simple, pungent garlic sauce, is the real, traditional accompaniment to mămăligă, real technique crushing the garlic with a little salt into a real smooth paste before thinning with oil and water.

name: Moldovan Ghiveci (Vegetable Stew)
description: Ghiveci, a real hearty lamb or goat and vegetable stew, is a genuine Moldovan regional staple, real technique cooking each vegetable long enough to soften without turning to mush.
steps_detailed: Brown the lamb, 6-7 minutes.
Add the eggplant, bell pepper, and carrot, and cook 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 25-28 minutes until everything is tender.

name: Moldovan Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and dill, reflecting Moldova's Dniester and Prut River fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and dill, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Moldovan Roasted Walnuts
description: A simple roasted walnut snack, walnuts being a significant Moldovan crop.
steps_detailed: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Moldovan Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Moldovan home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
